FAQs

## Frequently Asked Questions

[Sermorelin](https://www.gobymeds.com/#w-tabs-1-data-w-pane-0) [Weight Loss](https://www.gobymeds.com/#w-tabs-1-data-w-pane-1) [GobyMeds](https://www.gobymeds.com/#w-tabs-1-data-w-pane-2) [NAD+](https://www.gobymeds.com/#w-tabs-1-data-w-pane-3) [Account Info](https://www.gobymeds.com/#w-tabs-1-data-w-pane-4)

What is Sermorelin?

Sermorelin is a peptide therapy that stimulates natural growth hormone release. It may support energy, fat metabolism, sleep, and recovery.

How do I take injectable Sermorelin?

Typically injected subcutaneously at night, five days on, two days off. It must be taken on an empty stomach. At GobyMeds, Sermorelin is also offered as an oral tablet.

Is Sermorelin legal for wellness use?

Yes. Sermorelin is available for off-label use via prescription for anti-aging and vitality purposes.

Can Sermorelin help with weight loss?

Sermorelin has the potential to indirectly help with weight loss. Sermorelin may enhance fat metabolism and lean muscle support.

What are GLP-1 medications?

GLP-1 receptor agonists like semaglutide and tirzepatide mimic natural hormones that regulate appetite and blood sugar levels.

What is the difference between semaglutide and tirzepatide?

Semaglutide targets GLP-1 receptors. Tirzepatide targets both GLP-1 and GIP receptors.

Will my medication contain additives?

Possibly. Additives like B12, B6, NAD+, and glycine may be included to support comfort and minimize side effects.

‍

‍ **Niacin (Vitamin B3)**

Helps reduce fatigue and may support metabolic function.

‍ **Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6)**

Known for its anti-nausea properties. Often included to reduce queasiness—especially during early treatment phases.

‍ **Cyanocobalamin (Vitamin B12)**

A synthetic B12 used to support energy, red blood cell production, and metabolism. It's cost-effective and stable.

‍ **Methylcobalamin (Vitamin B12)**

The bioactive form of B12. Supports nerve health, brain clarity, and energy metabolism—no conversion needed in the liver.

‍ **NAD+ (Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide)**

A coenzyme that helps your cells generate energy. Added to reduce fatigue and support metabolic function.

‍ **Glycine**

An amino acid that may reduce injection site irritation and promote restful sleep. It also supports detox pathways and collagen synthesis.

These additives are selected by providers on a case-by-case basis depending on your individual needs and goals.

What are the side effects of GLP-1 and GLP-1/GIP medications?

Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, constipation, and appetite changes. Providers often use a “start low and go slow” approach to help minimize side effects.

Do compounded GLP-1 medications need to be refrigerated?

Yes. Store between 36°F and 46°F. Do not freeze. Use a cooler for travel.

Can I switch from tirzepatide to semaglutide OR semaglutide to tirzepatide?

Yes, with guidance from a licensed provider who may adjust dosing accordingly..

What is GobyMeds?

GobyMeds is a telehealth platform that offers personalized access to compounded semaglutide, compounded tirzepatide, NAD+, sermorelin, and other wellness-focused treatments. All prescriptions require consultation with a licensed provider.

Is GobyMeds legitimate?

Yes. GobyMeds is a legitimate telehealth provider, offering treatment plans under the supervision of licensed healthcare professionals.

Does GobyMeds offer brand-name weight loss medications?

Yes, GobyMeds offers brand-name medications including Zepbound, Mounjaro, Wegovy, and Ozempic.

Does GobyMeds have subscription fees or automatic refills?

No. GobyMeds does not charge any subscriptions fees or auto-renewals. We keep our prices transparent and easy to understand without any hidden fees. We offer up to 3 months of medication at a time.

What medications does GobyMeds offer?

GobyMeds offers compounded semaglutide, compounded tirzepatide, NAD+, sermorelin, and select brand-name medications.

What is NAD+?

NAD+ is a coenzyme critical to cellular energy production and metabolic health. It’s sometimes added to GLP-1 therapies to help reduce fatigue.

What are the possible side effects of NAD+?

Mild side effects can include nausea, flushing, dizziness, and localized irritation at the injection site.

Who should not take NAD+?

Those with active cancer, cardiovascular issues, severe liver/kidney conditions, or those pregnant/breastfeeding should avoid NAD+.

When will I be charged?

Your card is charged once a provider writes a prescription and is shipped from the pharmacy.

Can I cancel my GobyMeds order?

It depends on the order status. If your prescription has not been sent to the pharmacy, you may be able to cancel. Contact the support team via chat.

Can I change my shipping address?

Yes, if the order hasn’t shipped. Contact the support team via chat.

What forms of payment does GobyMeds accept?

All major credit cards and HSA/FSA cards are accepted. GobyMeds does not bill insurance.

Can I use my HSA/FSA at GobyMeds?

Yes. GobyMeds purchases are approved medical expenses. You can request a letter of medical necessity by contacting support.

Can I get a refund at GobyMeds?

No. Due to FDA regulations, all prescriptions are final sale and non-refundable.

Does GobyMeds offer discount codes?

Yes. If you have a valid discount code and it doesn’t work, contact the support team. To view active promotions, [click here.](https://www.gobymeds.com/legal/promotions)
